# `valueConfigs`: the dropdown value configs

Part of [generated data](../generated-data.md). `makeValueConfigs` must keep its `const` type parameter (the rule: [`src/01_SpreadsheetSchema/AGENTS.md`](../../src/01_SpreadsheetSchema/AGENTS.md)).

## How `valueConfigs` is generated

**`valueConfigs`** (`generated/valueConfigs.ts`) — generated by `ValueConfigOperator` (`05_Operators`) from the live "Value Config" sheet, once `columnConfigs` is already synced. After Column Config sync it still catalogs only distinct non-framework value titles in use, as Value Config headers; it asks Column Config for that title list, which walks identity rows (Table ID, Column ID) and reads each described column's live value title. **`makeValueConfigs` takes a `const` type parameter, and must keep it** (#18): without it the generated member lists infer as `string[]` and every dropdown column's value type collapses to bare `string`, which silently removes the union a switch over a Value Config's members is meant to be exhaustive against. The generated file carries no `as const` of its own, so the constructor is the only thing holding the literals. Measured at ~41k instantiations — see [type-check cost](../architecture/type-check-cost.md).

## The two kinds

Each entry is one of two kinds, and the value type and value schema of every column naming it follow the kind (#145):

- **A fixed list** is an array of members, each a string, number or boolean. The `const` parameter keeps it a literal tuple, so its value type is the union of its members, a number member staying a number literal, and its wire type is the union of their primitive kinds. Its value schema accepts only a member, and its default is its first member.
- **A live reference** is the marker `{ "kind": "liveReference" }`, with no members, because its options are rows added after the build. Its value type is `string`, and it takes the framework `string` value schema: any string is accepted, and its default is blank, so the column's **Empty value allowed** decides whether that blank reads. It never takes the `id` value schema, whose default throws.

`ValueConfigOperator` still emits only fixed lists of strings; the generator learns the rest from later #144 tickets. The framework's `valueKinds/` test program installs a hand-written config set with one of each.
